answer: A tundra supply depot gives each agent one anchor post driven into frozen ground at a numbered plot. Each season the keeper mixes a fresh pigment batch at the depot, paints a band on the post, and files a photo of the band beside a dated board. A neighboring keeper walks the plot that week and checks the band against the depot batch record; a moved post or a wrong batch darkens the plot for a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand driven posts and a thousand winter visits with matching pigment batches, so copying one photo buys nothing.
